beliefs.practice: Create a single MongoClient at application startup and reuse it for all requests (instantiate in FastAPI startup event and close in shutdown) and tune maxPoolSize to match your concurrency rather than creating per-request clients.

Keep the DocumentDB connection string and any API keys out of source control: read DOCUMENTDB_URI (and OPENAI_API_KEY) from environment variables in runtime, and use Azure Key Vault (or equivalent secret store) for production secrets instead of embedding them in files.
Enforce TLS/SSL for all client connections (use mongodb+srv:// or ?tls=true in the URI) and validate server certificates (do not set tlsAllowInvalidCertificates); fail fast if TLS validation fails.

Enable and rely on the driver's retryable writes and implement exponential-backoff retries for transient network or server errors (set retryWrites=true in the URI and catch transient exceptions to retry idempotent operations).

Configure sensible client timeouts to avoid stuck requests: set serverSelectionTimeoutMS, connectTimeoutMS and socketTimeoutMS appropriate to your network; don't rely on defaults that may hang under network partitions.

Create indexes that support the attribution aggregations: at minimum a compound index on (customer_id, event_time) (customer_id ASC, event_time ASC) and additional indexes on channel/source/type fields used for grouping or filtering.

Store attribution results as single per-customer documents and implement versioning with an incrementing version number updated atomically via findOneAndUpdate (or $inc) and enforce uniqueness with a compound unique index on (customer_id, version).

Prefer single-document atomic updates (upserts / findOneAndUpdate) for versioned writes to avoid multi-document transactions; only use multi-document transactions when absolutely necessary because of cost/latency.
Apply a data retention policy for raw events (for example a TTL index on event_time) so event collections don’t grow unbounded; tune expireAfterSeconds to your compliance and analytics needs.

When storing vectors, use a fixed-length float array field and create a dedicated vector index with an appropriate metric (cosine or L2) and HNSW/IVF parameters (e.g., m/efConstruction/efSearch) tuned for the latency/recall tradeoff; record the vector dimension in the schema for validation.
Optimize aggregation pipelines by pushing $match and $sort (on indexed fields) as early as possible and $project to remove unused fields early to reduce I/O and memory use during aggregation.
Set appropriate writeConcern/readConcern for attribution writes: use w='majority' (and a sensible wtimeoutMS) if you need durability across replicas; relax to w=1 for lower latency when acceptable.

Provision cluster capacity/tier to match query and indexing workload (monitor CPU, IOPS and memory) and leverage autoscaling or increase instance size if aggregations and vector search cause high load; validate on the live M30 cluster before relying on developer defaults.
Validate heavy queries and index usage using explain() and the provider’s management/inspection tools (the documentdb MCP tools) before deploying; iterate indexes based on actual explain plans.

For tests and local development use mocks or a separate test database (mongomock for unit tests and a dedicated test database on the cluster for integration tests); never run test seed scripts against production data.
Enforce idempotency for event ingestion by using an event_id and a unique index on event_id (or on customer_id+event_id) so repeated seed/rerun operations don't create duplicates.
Use server-side pagination and reasonable batchSize settings when reading large event sets for attribution (use cursors/limit+sort rather than loading entire collections into memory).

Instrument and emit operational metrics (query latencies, aggregation durations, index hit rates, connection pool metrics) and integrate with Azure Monitor/alerts so you detect regressions in throughput or slow attribution runs.
Redact or avoid persisting sensitive PII in logs and consider hashing or tokenizing customer identifiers when storing or exporting attribution data for analytics to meet privacy requirements.

Protect the LangChain/OpenAI integration: require OPENAI_API_KEY in env, validate presence at startup, never log the key, and implement rate-limiting and per-user quota controls for marketer-facing natural-language queries.
